//: Who may touch what, written down BEFORE anyone starts. Read docs/parallel-dev.md first, then BOTH briefs: docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md and docs/specs/adgrant-and-dev-agents.md. THIS IS PROGRAMME THREE, second half. Its first five parcels are landed and are kept in docs/parcels-programme-3-landed.json; programme two's thirteen are in docs/parcels-programme-2.json and programme one's nineteen in docs/parcels-programme-1.json. None of those three files is for running. Ownership freed by a retired parcel is reused here on purpose: adgrant-site inherits the AdGrant tree from adgrant-front, and booking-picker inherits the dialog from booking-dialog.
//brief: Two briefs, and a parcel reads the one its prompt names. unipile-rooms-and-booking.md carries the Unipile contract, the identity decisions and the rule that every inbound message is checked for who it is from, who it is to and which chat it is in. adgrant-and-dev-agents.md carries adgrant.ai's own content API, the six factual defects in the material being carried over, the split between generating a structure and uploading it, and the answer to the owner's question about per-agent limits. An agent that starts from a paraphrase instead will rebuild something that already exists or ship something that is wrong.
//seams: Files everything needs. A parcel may ADD up to three lines to one of these and delete none, and must declare which lines up front. Two one-line additions merge by keeping both; two thirty-line edits merge into something nobody can verify. THREE STATED EXCEPTIONS, carried over because the three-line grammar would make them unusable: scripts/build-kb.ts admits one appended Corpus const plus its name on the CORPORA line, shared/roster.ts admits one whole appended agent entry, and client/src/components/site/doors/bodies.tsx admits one door-to-body entry. All three are appends at the end of a list, which is the shape that merges. A FOURTH, added for programme three: shared/schema.ts admits one re-export line. A new table is fifteen lines and the seam allows three, so a parcel that needs a table writes it in its OWN file and re-exports it from the schema - drizzle-kit follows the export, and one line merges where fifteen do not.
//frozen: Nobody edits these during a parallel run. A change here invalidates every parcel at once. Programme three has one consequence worth stating: client/index.html carries the one <head> this application serves, so a second site on a second host cannot have its own title and meta without editing a frozen file. That is why adgrant-front builds a route tree and not a second host - the host switch is owner work, done when no wave is running.
//alone: Parcels marked runAlone touch the room, the panel or the shell - everything reads those, and two agents in them at once produce a merge nobody can check. One agent, let it finish, then start the others.
//order: The waves are in scripts/build-prompts.mjs and check-parcels.mjs reads them back. Programme three's ordering is a dependency chain, not a preference, and it has three links. (1) unipile-core is wave one ALONE because four parcels import its client; a parcel that writes its own Unipile client because the shared one did not exist yet is four incompatible error mappers. (2) booking-server and booking-dialog are the same wave and build to the request and response shapes fixed in the brief's section 3 - that is what fixing them in writing was for. (3) room-identity precedes login-create-room, because the claim dialog the site's new menu opens is the one room-identity builds. Beyond the chain, one standing rule: AT MOST ONE PARCEL PER WAVE MAY TOUCH server/routes.ts. Three parcels here need a route, and they are in three different waves for that reason alone.

adgrant-site.why: The AdGrant.AI front page and shell exist from an earlier wave, built from what the repository already knew. Now there is the real material - 23 written pages, 12 starter templates and a measured statistic over 4,539 accounts - and the owner wants the four sections rebuilt in this design system, with AdGrant.AI's own mark, menu and footer, and the front page turned from a form into a conversation.
adgrant-site.done: A four-section site in the top-rated.team design system wearing AdGrant.AI's own chrome. THE SECTIONS, named as the live site names them: Ad Grant Glossary (Terminology explained), Case Studies, Tips & Tricks (Custom workarounds), Starter Templates. Each gets an index and a leaf page, rendered from shared/adgrant.ts, which the previous wave generated. KEEP THE URL SHAPES - /glossary/<slug>, /tricks/<slug> and their siblings - because every page carries relatedLinks into the others and the internal link graph is worth more than a tidier path. SET TITLE AND DESCRIPTION PER ROUTE from each page's own metaTitle and metaDescription, the way client/src/pages/landing.tsx does it. The live site serves one title and one canonical for all 74 URLs and injects the rest client-side, so this metadata exists and is currently wasted; this is the cheapest real improvement on the whole site. THE FRONT PAGE: the measured statistic goes on it. 4,539 Ad Grant accounts processed, 16,575 campaigns, 3,142,469 keywords, with the medians beside them - that is the most valuable thing this product owns and the current site does almost nothing with it. State what each number is a number OF, and do not round it into a marketing figure. Then the conversation: the front page's action is an agent that asks what the nonprofit needs, not a form. Identity is required before it generates, and generating is the previous wave's endpoint - call it, do not reimplement it, and print the remaining count of three where a person can see it before they spend one. Say plainly what happens: a structure is produced and shown, and a person sets up the account link afterwards. Do NOT write any sentence implying the structure was uploaded into their Google Ads account. THE CHROME: its own mark, its own top menu, its own footer, both linking back to top-rated.team. Extend the accent and wordmark in client/src/components/site/doors/adgrant-style.ts rather than starting a second palette; the type scale, the spacing scale and the class vocabulary in client/src/components/site/doors/quiet.ts stay exactly as they are. No import of the site's Header or Footer. Build it so it can move to its own host later: nothing that assumes the apex. Two faces of type, not the twenty-eight the live site loads; no pinch-zoom lock; and no machine-translation gadget - English only is an honest state. Where a section's material is thin, say less rather than padding it.

room-login.why: The owner has asked three times for one control and it is still not on the site: with nothing remembered a visitor sees 'Open a room' and no way back into a room they already have. The previous attempt shipped an email form labelled 'Send a link' beside it, which is neither the label nor the position he asked for, and it was sealed before it ever answered a request because it could be made to mail a stranger a working link into a room somebody else controls. So this parcel is both the feature and the repair, and they are one parcel because they are the same code.
room-login.done: LOGIN | OPEN A ROOM, and it works three ways. START BY READING the sealed block at the top of the room-access routes in server/routes.ts — it names the three defects that put it there — and then `git show waves-11-12-wip:server/room-access.ts` and `:client/src/components/site/RoomMenu.tsx`, which are the previous attempt. Most of the email half is written and correct; take it, do not start again. THE CONTROL. With nothing remembered the pair reads LOGIN | Open a room, in that order — LOGIN first, because a returning visitor is the one who needs it and 'Open a room' is what a new one presses anyway. With rooms remembered it stays Your rooms | Open a room, unchanged. LOGIN opens one panel offering the ways that actually work on THIS deployment and never a way that does not: LinkedIn, WhatsApp, or a link to an address. THE THREE WAYS. (1) An address, which is the sealed code, repaired — see below. (2) LinkedIn, and (3) WhatsApp, both of which need something that does not exist yet: identity-store.ts can only answer getBinding(workspaceId), a FORWARD lookup, and login is the reverse question — given this person, which rooms are theirs. Build that index in server/room-login.ts over the same hashed identifiers the bindings already store, so no new personal data is written: a LinkedIn subject and the peppered WhatsApp chat hash are already what identity keeps. WHATSAPP IS HOUSE-ONLY, the same rule as the booking gate, for the same reason — shared/roster.ts WHATSAPP_URL is the owner's personal mobile and this repository is public. Use HOUSE_HOSTS from shared/operator.ts, decided where a fork cannot reach around it. A FORK SEES LinkedIn and the address link, and the panel simply does not draw the third. THE REPAIRS, each of which is a reason the current code is sealed. (a) AUTHORISATION. sendRoomAccessLink finds rooms through workspaces.visitorEmail, which is self-asserted: an anonymous caller opens a room, sets visitorEmail to a stranger's address, and asks us to mail that stranger a link into the attacker's room, from our domain and our sender. Stop reading that field for this purpose. An address earns a room only through bindRoomAddress, and bindRoomAddress must acquire real callers — the LinkedIn userinfo email, and an address a person typed INTO a room they were already inside — because today it has none, which is also why the feature cannot find anything. (b) DURABILITY. Issued links and address bindings are process-local Maps, so a restart inside the hour turns a live link into 'already been used', while the mail and ROOM_ACCESS_SPENT_LINE both promise an hour. Rows in shared/schema-rooms.ts, hashed as they are now. Without a database the feature reports itself unavailable rather than promising an hour it cannot keep. (c) THE MAILED URL must not be built from the Host header. publicBaseUrl(req) falls back to it when PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset, and a link mailed to a victim can then point at an attacker's server. No PUBLIC_BASE_URL, no mail. (d) THE IDENTICAL REPLY the brief requires is currently defeated by latency — the no-room path returns at once and the room-found path waits on the mail provider. Make the timing say nothing either. (e) THE PROVIDER-REJECTS branch is untested and tells the visitor a link was sent when none was; test it. UNSEAL by deleting the guard block in the same commit, and only once every item above is true. THE REPLY ON SCREEN STAYS IDENTICAL whether or not a room was found — a form that says 'no room for that address' tells anybody whether a given person is a customer here.

server/routes.ts: the booking sign-in routes, replacing the sealed block
shared/api.ts: what the popup learns about a signed-in booker

booking-signin-fix.why: The LinkedIn half of the booking popup was written, reviewed and sealed. The button on screen is still hardcoded disabled and no client code calls the route, so every branch of it is unreachable; and the branch that matters most — LinkedIn declining to give us an address — writes a calendar event nobody can be reached about, including on forks where the identical booking is refused outright. This finishes it and connects it.
booking-signin-fix.done: THE BUTTON WORKS, AND THE BRANCH BEHIND IT IS RIGHT. Read the sealed block in server/routes.ts first; it names why this is off. Then section 3.1 of docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md. (1) NO ADDRESS FROM LINKEDIN IS THE NORMAL CASE, not an error: LinkedIn documents email and email_verified as optional and the claim is absent until the product is provisioned. That booking must land EXACTLY where a booking with the field left blank lands — the hold from server/booking/hold.ts, a wa.me code, and no calendar write until the message proves it. Today it calls createBookingEvent immediately with attendees: [] and notify: false, which is a call in the owner's calendar with no way to reach the other person and nothing that can ever confirm or remind it. BookingLinkedInResult has no member that can carry a hold; give it one. The test that asserts the current shape asserts the defect. (2) THE HOST DECIDES, as it does for the typed path: writeSignedInBooking never sees a host, so on a fork it creates precisely the address-less booking POST /api/booking refuses there with ADDRESS_REQUIRED_LINE. Thread the host through and use whatsappGateAllowed. (3) THE RETURN PATH IS AN OPEN REDIRECT: sanitizeBookingReturnPath rejects a leading // but not a path that normalises into one, so the Location can be made protocol-relative and the visitor's email handed to whoever owns that host. (4) THE SESSION IS AN UNAUTHENTICATED BEARER TOKEN for a name, an address and a LinkedIn profile, delivered in a URL query and readable for fifteen minutes by anyone who sees it — a referrer header, a shared link, a browser history. Spend it on first read. (5) THE ROOM-BINDING GUARD IS VACUOUS: the four assertions that prove a booking sign-in never becomes a room claim look the binding up under a workspace id no code path can produce, so they pass whatever signin.ts writes. Make them look where the write would actually land. (6) THE MISSING TESTS, each a branch that exists and has no case: an expired or replayed state, a token exchange LinkedIn refuses, and a slot taken by a hold rather than by a calendar event while the visitor was away at LinkedIn. (7) CONNECT IT. The button in BookingDialog.tsx is hardcoded disabled with its own sentence; it must ask the server whether sign-in is available, carry the visitor's pick into the round trip, restore that pick on the way back, and re-check the slot is still free before writing. Inert without LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID: one sentence on the disabled button, read from the server, and the other two ways stay on screen. (8) FIX THE PROSE that these defects made false — the header of signin.ts and the contract in shared/api.ts both say the no-address sign-in performs 'the same write as no address at all', and no address at all performs no write. NEVER SEND A LINKEDIN MESSAGE: signing in is a way to hand over an address, not a channel to write on, and a reminder there is the unsolicited automation the pending API application says this product does not do. UNSEAL by deleting the guard in the same commit, once the above is true.
